newsitem.title: USA: Grigsby, Gary firms ousted from Dade Cty, Fla deal.
newsitem.headline: Grigsby, Gary firms ousted from Dade Cty, Fla deal.

text.p: Bond firms owned by California's Calvin Grigsby and Miami's Howard Gary were removed from an $80 million deal by the Dade County, Fla., Expressway Authority because of news reports linking them to an alleged corruption investigation, officials involved in the deal said Wednesday.
Representatives of Howard Gary & Co and Grigsby and Associates both protested the decision at an expressway authority meeting Tuesday, according to others who attended.
An official at Howard Gary & Co declined to comment Wednesday. Grigsby did not immediately return calls.
County finance officials were unavailable for comment.

The Miami Herald reported in September that the FBI videotaped a meeting in which Grigsby, Gary and Dade County Commissioner James Burke discussed alleged kickbacks in connection with a Dade bond deal.
None of the three have been charged with wrongdoing and neither the FBI nor the U.S. Attorney's Office would comment on their ongoing investigation into the allegations.

Nonetheless, the expressway deal was the second in which Gary's firm was removed from a Dade County syndicate because of concerns that disclosure involving the investigation could affect the county's borrowing rate.
Earlier, Dade County commissioners removed Howard Gary & Co from a $30 million seaport revenue bond issue. AIBC Investment Corp replaced the firm as senior manager for that deal.

Additionally, Dade County Housing Finance Authority scheduled a meeting Thursday to discuss disclosure issues stemming from the role of Howard Gary & Co as financial adviser for an upcoming bond issue by that agency.

Grigsby and Associates is still desginated as senior manager on an upcoming $183 million Dade County revenue bond issue for a new basketball arena, but that deal is on hold pending a Tuesday referendum on the financing plan.

The variable rate, taxable expressway revenue bond issue is scheduled for pricing the week of Nov 20. It will be the first debt issued by the expressway authority, which was recently formed to manage two toll roads and two causeways in Dade County. Bond proceeds will be used to acquire the roads and bridges from the state, with debt service paid from tolls.
